Backend: 32/32 pytest tests PASSED (auth, products, recipe, bundles, pin map, QC template, cable functions, machine programs, full WO flow including batch colors with warna_wajib + alasan validation, mark-cutting-done, bundle detail nav, QC submit Pass/Fail->WO status, role enforcement, user CRUD, dashboard stats, change-password). Work Order creation via UI works (WO-20260627-001 created). However, WorkOrderDetail page is STUCK on 'Memuat...' loading state due to a bug in load() — Promise.all references `cs` inside one of its own array elements before the array is resolved, making it always undefined, which triggers the early return. This blocks all WO-detail UI tests (cutting sheet UI, batch colors UI, bundle labels UI, QC submit UI, print buttons inside detail). Print pages (deep-linked /work-orders/{wo}/print/*) DO load (they fetch data independently).

ui_bugs.issue: Page stuck on 'Memuat...' for ALL work orders. The 4th element of Promise.all uses cs?.data?.wo?.product_sku but `cs` is the array element name that is only bound AFTER Promise.all resolves; at definition time it is undefined. Then .catch(()=>[]) swallows the rejection and returns []. Destructuring const [cs,...]=[] makes cs undefined, triggering the early return `if (!cs) return;`. Page never renders tabs/data.
Recipe TableRow lacks data-testid="cable-row-{code}" (only count is verifiable via tbody tr). Spec listed this testid.

Spec lists nav testids as nav-products/nav-work-orders but Layout.jsx generates them as nav--products / nav--work-orders (double dash because path starts with `/`). Works but is misleading and not what the spec referenced.

critical_code_review_comments: WorkOrderDetail.jsx load() is a textbook race-condition bug. Promise.all array literal evaluates all 4 promises synchronously; the inner reference to `cs` inside element index 3 uses the outer (undefined) variable, not the resolved value. Combined with `.catch(() => [])` it silently masks the failure. This made every WO unusable in the UI.
Swallowing fetch errors with `.catch(() => [])` everywhere prevents users (and devs) from seeing real failures. At minimum log e or toast.
Layout.jsx nav testid generation produces ugly `nav--products` (double dash) from `to.replace(/[\/]/g, '-')` when path starts with `/`. Should strip leading `/` first.
WorkOrderDetail.jsx is large (~386 lines) — consider splitting Cutting Sheet, Bundle Labels, QC, Pin Map sections into separate sub-components.

rca_of_the_issue: WorkOrderDetail.jsx line 34-39: Promise.all([... , api.get(`/work-orders/${woNumber}`).then(() => api.get(`/products/${(cs?.data?.wo?.product_sku) || ''}/pin-map`).catch(() => ({data: []})) ]).catch(() => []). The reference `cs` inside the .then() is the const declared as the destructuring target on the left of `=` and is undefined until Promise.all resolves. So /products//pin-map is requested → 404 → Promise.all rejects → outer .catch returns []. Then `const [cs,b,q,pm] = []` → all undefined → `if (!cs) return;` → page stays on Memuat... forever for every WO.
